project-charter.title: Observe the Leaf Spring Suspension

cards.title: Client Brief & Application Context
cards.body: Tata Motors Commercial Vehicle Chassis Division has assigned you to analyze the construction and verify the basic design of a rear semi-elliptic multi-leaf spring assembly for a medium commercial vehicle.

cards.title: Real-World Operating Parameters
cards.body: The rear axle carries a total payload force of 40 kN, supported symmetrically by two identical multi-leaf spring assemblies (20 kN central load per spring). Students must verify bending stress, deflection, and Factor of Safety under maximum static axle load.

cards.title: Engineering Objectives & Scope
items: Observe commercial vehicle leaf spring construction and trace the load path.
Label leaf spring assembly components on Engineering Asset EA-13.
Establish the simplified cantilever beam engineering model for multi-leaf springs.
Determine maximum bending stress, spring deflection, and actual Factor of Safety.
Render an engineering judgement and design modification recommendation.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EA-13 Project Charter for Leaf Spring Design Verification.

component-identification.title: Identify Leaf Spring Components
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset showing commercial vehicle multi-leaf spring assembly and mounting hardware.

labels.feedback: Longest top leaf with formed spring eyes carrying eye pin bushings.
Stack of progressively shorter spring leaves providing uniform bending strength.
Front eyelet connected directly to chassis front hanger bracket.
Rear eye connected to pivoting shackle accommodating spring length change during deflection.
Central clamping pin holding leaves in alignment and locating spring on axle seat.
U-shaped threaded rods clamping the spring assembly securely to the axle.
Machined mounting pad on axle housing supporting the spring centre.
Commercial vehicle rear axle housing transmitting load to road wheels.

leaf-construction.title: Understand Leaf Spring Construction
leaf-construction.prompt: Multi-leaf springs consist of one master leaf and several graduated leaves of decreasing length clamped together.

mcq.question: Why are multi-leaf springs constructed with leaves of progressively decreasing lengths from top to bottom?

options.label: To approximate a beam of uniform strength, maintaining uniform bending stress along the entire spring length while saving material weight.
To allow the top leaf to snap easily during heavy impacts.
To create space for internal hydraulic oil flow between leaves.
To ensure shorter leaves carry 100% of the load while the master leaf carries zero load.

load-path.title: Understand the Load Path
load-path.prompt: Analyze the load path through the commercial vehicle rear suspension system.

mcq.question: Which sequence correctly describes the primary load transmission path from vehicle chassis to road wheels?

options.label: Chassis Frame → Spring Eyes & Hanger/Shackle → Multi-Leaf Spring → Axle Seat & U-Bolts → Axle → Wheels
Wheels → Master Leaf → Chassis Frame → Graduated Leaves → U-Bolts → Axle Seat
Axle → Centre Bolt → Front Eye → Chassis Frame → Wheels → Shackle
Graduated Leaves → Centre Bolt → Chassis Frame → Spring Eyes → Axle Seat → Wheels

engineering-model.title: Establish the Engineering Model
given: Total Rear Axle Payload (W_axle) = 40.0 kN (40,000 N)
Number of Leaf Springs per Axle = 2
Central Load per Leaf Spring (2P) = 40.0 / 2 = 20.0 kN (20,000 N)
End Reaction Force at each Eye Pin (P) = 20.0 / 2 = 10.0 kN (10,000 N)

design-requirements.title: Establish Design Requirements
given: Total Number of Leaves (n) = 10 (nf = 2 full length, ng = 8 graduated)
Modulus of Elasticity for Steel (E) = 207,000 N/mm²

deflection-safety-check.title: Verify Deflection and Factor of Safety

formulas.name: Spring Deflection (delta)
formulas.formula: \delta = \frac{6 P L^3}{E n b t^3} = \frac{6 \times 10000 \times 500^3}{207000 \times 10 \times 60 \times 8^3} = 117.94 \text{ mm}

options.title: ACCEPT DESIGN AS ADEQUATE FOR REGULAR PAYLOAD
options.description: Calculated bending stress (781.25 N/mm²) remains below material yield strength (900 N/mm²), providing FoS = 1.15 under peak static load.

options.title: REJECT / INCREASE NUMBER OF LEAVES TO 12 OR THICKNESS TO 9 MM
options.description: Under severe off-road dynamic shock loads (1.5x static bump), FoS = 1.15 is insufficient. Increasing number of leaves n to 12 or leaf thickness t to 9 mm reduces bending stress to 650 N/mm² and raises FoS to 1.38.
